transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I’m constantly forgetting little everyday things—appointments, errands, even finishing what I start for the community center. My husband and friends got so worried that they thought I might be developing early dementia, but my regular doctor suggested it could actually be a long-standing attention issue.
Have these attention and forgetfulness problems been present since childhood or the teen years, or did they start only recently in adulthood?

They actually go all the way back to my childhood, though they've only really started causing major problems over the past two years since I retired and lost my structured routine. When I was little, my report cards always said I was bright but would daydream, rush, and talk out of turn, and my mother constantly scolded me for leaving chores half-done to wander off. These tendencies have always been there, but without a set schedule, they've really caught up with me lately.
Do you also have trouble sitting still, feel restless, or interrupt or blurt things out before thinking, or is it mainly forgetfulness and distractibility?

Yes, it is definitely more than just forgetfulness. I struggle a lot with restlessness, like constantly tapping my foot or feeling an urge to get up and do things even when I'm trying to relax. I also have a bad habit of interrupting people in our committee meetings and jumping in to finish their sentences before they are done.
Do these attention and restlessness problems cause clear difficulties in more than one area of your life, such as at home, in social situations, or in volunteer/work activities?

Yes, they definitely affect both my home life and my volunteering at the community center. At the center, I've let people down by forgetting supplies and mixing up dates, to the point where others have suggested I step back from leading projects. At home, it causes a lot of worry and frustration because I double-book events, forget errands, and struggle to keep our household routine organized.
Did these attention and restlessness symptoms begin before age 12 and continue consistently through childhood, or were there long periods when they were not a problem?

Yes, they definitely started well before age 12 and were quite consistent throughout my childhood. Back in elementary school, my report cards always noted that I was bright but would "daydream, rush, and talk out of turn." My mother also constantly scolded me for never finishing my chores because I'd wander off halfway through to do something else.
Do you have mostly inattention, mostly hyperactivity/impulsivity, or a combination of both? Please tell me which symptoms are the biggest problem for you now and in childhood.

It definitely feels like a combination of both. Currently, my biggest struggles are forgetting everyday tasks and losing track of projects, alongside feeling constantly on the go and interrupting others in meetings. Back in childhood, it was a similar mix of daydreaming and rushing, while also talking out of turn and wandering off from my chores.

final_diagnosis.reason: Long-standing childhood-onset pattern of inattention and hyperactivity/impulsivity with clear persistence into adulthood, causing impairment in multiple settings (home and volunteering). Symptoms include daydreaming, losing track of tasks, forgetting appointments/errands, restlessness, interrupting, talking out of turn, and leaving chores unfinished. This is most consistent with ADHD, predominantly combined presentation as coded in ICD-10 as F90.0.
